topic.title: Rich vs poor: the same $5,000 year-end bonus

title: Poor buys the TV. Rich buys the shop 📺
description:
Where does a $5,000 bonus really go?
One spends it on a TV, one puts it in an index fund at an assumed 7% a year: checked after 10, 20 and 30 years, computed. The return is an assumption, not a promise; no fund named. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: TV or the shop: which one are you? Comment

lines.text: His bonus bought a TV. Mine bought a slice of the companies selling it.
Both got $5,000. Three check-ins, and the last one stings.
I went straight to the store. Biggest screen they had, plus a sound bar. Bonus, gone in a day.
I put mine in an index fund. A tiny slice of a whole market of companies, the TV shops included.
Check-in one, after 10 years. At an assumed 7% a year, my bonus is $9,836.
Meanwhile, my TV? Scratched, slow, and nobody wants to buy it.
Check-in two, 20 years in: $19,348. And my money tree is speeding up.
My TV finally died. Straight into the bin.
Check-in three, 30 years: $38,061. That whole tree grew from one bonus I never touched.
So that TV never really cost $5,000. It cost Rohan $38,061.
Poor people buy the thing. Rich people buy a piece of the people selling it.
Next bonus? I'm buying the shop, not the screen.
